newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening slightly higher.

text.p: New York precious metals futures are called to open slightly higher Monday after a test of support levels in gold and silver in bullion trade overnight.
COMEX December gold was called unchanged to up $0.30 from Friday's finish of $388.80 an ounce after trading between $388.90 and $389.20 on overnight ACCESS.
Spot gold was fixed in London this morning at $385.00 versus Friday's close in New York at $384.85/385.35.
COMEX gold warehouse stocks were unchanged Friday at 1,398,134 ounces.
Both gold and silver ended lower Friday for the eighth day in a row despite the threat of inflation revealed in the stronger-than-expected U.S. August jobs data.
COMEX December silver is called unchanged to up 1.00 cent from Friday's close of $5.158, after trading between $5.140 and $5.170 on ACCESS.
COMEX silver stocks rose 717,152 ounces Friday to 150,913,191 ounces.
Both December gold and December silver are seen testing support again around $388.00 and $5.150, respectively, with the July/August recovery now possibly over, traders said.
NYMEX October platinum and NYMEX December palladium are called little changed from Friday's closes of $396.40 and $126.75, respectively.
But unease about U.S. bond and equity markets and the forthcoming US elections may help to provide support for precious metals, analysts said.
